title: Semen Analysis: 5 in 100 Future Dads Are 'Below Normal'? #Shorts
description:
Where do semen analysis "normal ranges" come from? The WHO gathered results from thousands of men, across five continents, whose partners had gotten pregnant within a year. The reference limit is drawn at the 5th centile: by definition, 5 future dads out of 100 sit below it. That line is not a fertility cut-off. Dr Senai Aksoy explains.

▶ Full video: https://youtu.be/TluWIqqgQiw

On-screen references: WHO, laboratory manual for the examination of human semen, 6th edition (2021) · Campbell MJ, et al. Andrology 2021, PMID 33528873

This content is for information only. It does not replace an individual medical evaluation.
English-dubbed version with an AI voice based on Dr Aksoy's own voice; AI-assisted lip synchronization.

title: Testosterone and Sperm: Booster or Handbrake? #Shorts
description:
"Just take some testosterone, it'll put nitro in the tank"? The opposite. The WHO tested injectable testosterone as male contraception: in their 1990 study, nearly six out of ten men ended up with zero sperm. The guidelines are categorical: never use testosterone to boost a semen analysis. If you take it, even "just for the gym", tell your doctor. Dr Senai Aksoy explains.

▶ Full video: https://youtu.be/TluWIqqgQiw

On-screen references: WHO Task Force, Lancet 1990, PMID 1977002 · NICE NG257, Fertility problems (2026)
